grounding_quotes: The "/customers" endpoint accepts HTTP POST requests to create a customer for the authenticated user.

functional_test_entanglement.explanation: All five functional tests operate under a single identity (create_customer/store_token/authorize are called without an alternate header set). None registers a second account or asserts that one account's customer or token is unreachable from another, so the per-account scoping rule is asserted by no functional test.

grounding_quotes: HTTP GET requests to "/charges" list the authenticated user's charge history and may include an optional "customerId" query parameter to filter results by customer.

functional_test_entanglement.explanation: func_test_authorize_charge_and_list_history lists unfiltered and asserts its OWN charge is PRESENT; func_test_list_charge_history_filtered_by_customer asserts the filter works within one account. Neither asserts that another account's charge is ABSENT, because the functional suite never creates a second account. Removing the ownership qualifier therefore does not make any functional test punish unrequired behaviour.

grounding_quotes: On success, the server responds with status code 201 and returns a PaymentToken object containing "id", "customerId", "brand", "masked", "expMonth", and "expYear".
The API allows users to create customers, store masked payment tokens for those customers, authorize charges against stored tokens, void pending charges, and retrieve charge history.

functional_test_entanglement.explanation: func_test_create_customer_store_and_list_tokens stores a token and lists tokens, but asserts only that the documented fields are present; it never asserts the submitted opaque token value is absent from any response.

api_twin.location: api_spec components.schemas.PaymentToken — enumerates masked and omits token (structural)
api_twin.quote: PaymentToken: properties: id, customerId, brand, masked, expMonth, expYear

layer_reason: The specification states no obligation not to echo the stored token. What grounds this check is the documented PaymentToken response shape — it carries "masked" and never the submitted value — which is an A-con data contract that R3(3) forbids removing. Grounding is A-con and the sentence stays: layer (ii) negative control.

ablation.original_text: On success, the server responds with status code 201 and returns a PaymentToken object containing "id", "customerId", "brand", "masked", "expMonth", and "expYear".
ablation.note: Response-shape contract, not a security obligation. Parallel to BeginnerLoginNotes/sec_test_insufficiently_protected_credentials_auth_response: both credential-exposure checks turn out to be anchored in A-con response shapes, so both serve as negative controls rather than main-analysis items.
